encounters.cc: Painless bilateral ankle swelling following addition of amlodipine for blood pressure control

lines: Painless bilateral ankle swelling following addition of amlodipine for blood pressure control

This 74-year-old male with primary adrenal insufficiency and benign prostatic hyperplasia, previously evaluated in Endocrinology and Urology, returns with concerns regarding bilateral lower extremity swelling.
His blood pressure was poorly controlled on hydrochlorothiazide alone, so amlodipine was added to his regimen 6 weeks ago.
Since then, his systolic pressure has improved from 168 mm Hg to 132 mm Hg, and he reports generally feeling better.
However, he has developed painless bilateral ankle swelling that worsens by the end of the day and improves slightly overnight.
- Transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) 3 years prior
His medications include amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, and aspirin.
He does not use NSAIDs or steroids.
- Quetiapine 200 mg PO daily at bedtime
- Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO daily after evening meal
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning, 10 mg PO every evening
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 15 years ago (30 pack-year history).
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
He denies dyspnea, chest pain, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.
On exam, vital signs are normal
There is 2+ pitting edema bilaterally in the lower extremities.
Jugular venous pressure is normal, and heart and lung exams are unremarkable.
There is no hepatomegaly or ascites.
Labs including renal function, albumin, and BNP are all within normal limits.
Echocardiogram from 3 months ago showed normal left ventricular function.
The clinician suspects the edema is related to the patient's antihypertensive medication.

lines: Bulge on lower left side of abdomen noticed when standing or straining

He denies any trauma, prior abdominal surgery, or heavy lifting.
He reports no abdominal pain, changes in bowel habits, nausea, or weight loss.
His medical history includes hypertension and osteoarthritis.
- Transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) 3 years prior
